title: The court's role in appointing an arbitrator when parties disagree
p1:
What happens when two parties agree to arbitration but cannot agree on the person who will decide the dispute?

Many assume the arbitration process ends there. It doesn't. The law has a solution when the appointment process breaks down.
p2:
A common misconception is that courts choose an arbitrator like a judge deciding the entire dispute. The court's role is much narrower.

When parties fail to appoint an arbitrator as agreed, the court can step in and help complete the appointment process. It ensures that arbitration can begin instead of getting stuck at the first step.
p3:
The interesting part: the court is not deciding who is right or wrong in the underlying conflict. It is only helping create the forum where the dispute will be resolved.

The practical takeaway? A disagreement over the arbitrator does not automatically defeat an arbitration clause. The mechanism for moving forward still exists.
conclusion: Have you seen a contract where the arbitration clause looked strong, but the appointment process created problems? What should parties focus on while drafting such clauses?
